Your job will be to take what works, keep the speed and experimentation that made it successful, and progressively make the underlying platform simpler, more robust and easier for other developers to understand and operate.

You should be equally comfortable using an AI coding agent to build an application in an afternoon and opening the resulting codebase to work out how it actually works.

  • Own and evolve the CUBE platform, becoming the primary developer responsible for its architecture, codebase, developer experience, reliability and ongoing operation.

Optics11 is a fast-growing high-tech company based in Amsterdam, developing advanced fiber optic sensing systems for the most demanding environments. Our technology detects the earliest signs of failure in critical assets – from high-voltage energy infrastructure to subsea and defense applications – and gives our customers precise, real-time data they can act on.

The Role

As Senior Product Designer you shape how our customers and operators experience Optics11’s end-to-end underwater security solutions: from in-field sensor data acquisition, through data processing, to the software platform where that data is exposed and acted on. You combine user research with hands-on UX/UI design: you understand users in the field, turn those insights into workflows and interface designs, and hand over clear, build-ready designs to our front-end developers. You are part of the Product team in Underwater Security and work closely with Product Management, R&D, Engineering, Data Science, Software, Sales, Projects and Application Engineering.

No two weeks will look the same. You might join an Application Engineer in the field, interview operators and technicians, trace how sensor data flows from the field to the operator’s screen, prototype a new workflow in Figma, or review a front-end implementation with the developers. You own the user experience of our software platform, from research insight to interface design, and make sure real user needs guide decisions across technical, product and commercial teams.

Within your first 6–12 months, you will establish a shared, evidence-based view of our users through personas, journey maps and a structured insight repository; evolve our design system and UI guidelines for the software platform; and deliver interface designs for priority platform features that our developers can build with confidence. This reduces development risk and helps us deliver technology customers can trust in demanding, high-stakes environments

Responsibilities

  • Lead user and customer research: plan and run qualitative, quantitative and field studies across installation, operation and maintenance (for example alongside our Application Engineers), and translate findings into product and design decisions.

  • Design the user experience of our software platform: turn product requirements from Product Management and the Product Owner into information architecture, user flows and interaction patterns for complex, data-rich operator workflows (detect, assess, identify and classify), from early concepts to interactive prototypes.

  • Propose and hand over UI designs to front-end developers: create high-fidelity, build-ready designs and specifications, align on feasibility with developers and the Product Owner, and review implementations for quality and consistency.

  • Own end-to-end customer journeys: map the experience from in-field deployment and data acquisition through data processing to the software platform, including demo flows and supporting internal processes.

  • Manage personas and customer insights: maintain the persona set and a central research repository, and synthesise learnings collected across the organisation.

  • Validate and measure outcomes: run usability tests before and after release, define adoption and usability metrics, and report impact to stakeholders.

  • Evolve and maintain our design system: extend the existing basis with UI components, patterns and guidelines that keep the platform consistent, accessible and efficient to develop.

  • Partner across the organisation: work closely with Product Management, Product Ownership and System Architecture, as well as Sales, Business Development, Application Engineering, Support and Marketing, to prioritise development, reduce product risk and advance user-centred practices.


Requirements

  • Master’s degree in interaction design, human-computer interaction, computer science or a related field, or equivalent experience.

  • 5+ years of experience in UX or product design, covering both user research and hands-on UX/UI design, preferably in defense or other technical, high-stakes industries.

  • A portfolio showing end-to-end work, from research and workflows to high-fidelity UX/UI for data-rich professional software (e.g. situational-awareness, control-room or analytics applications).

  • Experience working on integrated software platforms rather than isolated websites or prototypes.

  • Experience handing designs over to front-end developers and working with and evolving a design system, with a working understanding of front-end technology and its constraints.

  • Proficiency in qualitative and quantitative research methods, with the ability to translate data into actionable insights and design proposals.

  • Understanding of end-to-end systems in which sensor data is acquired in the field, processed and exposed on a software platform, ideally in complex or regulated environments.

  • Able to translate complex technical workflows and data into clear, intuitive interfaces, with strong attention to visual detail, consistency and quality.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English; able to present research and designs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Proficiency in Figma and in research and collaboration tools such as Jira Product Discovery, Dovetail and Miro.

  • Willingness to travel and do field research.

  • Driver’s license B (or international equivalent).

  • Ability to pass a background / security screening by the Dutch AIVD/MIVD, as you will be working with clients in the defense industry.

Nice to Have

  • Big plus: Experience with underwater acoustics or sonar software.

  • Plus: Experience in design leadership, or in setting up design practices in a growing organisation.

  • Plus: Front-end skills (e.g. HTML/CSS, React) for prototyping next to AI based tooling.

  • Plus: Proficiency in Dutch.


Screening

You will work with clients in the defense and security sectors. Obtaining a Certificate of No Objection issued by the AIVD, the Dutch General Intelligence and Security Service, is mandatory. This means you will need to undergo a security screening. We will explain the process and guide you through the applicable requirements.

What we’re all about.

Do you ever have the urge to do things better than the last time? We do. And it’s this urge that drives us every day. Our environment of discovery and innovation means we’re able to create deep and valuable relationships with our clients to create real change for them and their industries. It’s what got us here – and it’s what will make our future. At Quantexa, you’ll experience autonomy and support in equal measures allowing you to form a career that matches your ambitions. 41% of our colleagues come from an ethnic or religious minority background. We speak over 20 languages across our 47 nationalities, creating a sense of belonging for all.

AI is changing the engineering industry, and we see it as a huge opportunity to deliver more value to our customers, at unprecedented scale and pace, and to a higher standard than ever before. We want to be at the forefront of this change as we become an AI-native engineering organisation.

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help lead this change and shape the next generation of products that transform how organisations around the world use data. You'll join our R&D department, over 200 people across London, Ireland and Malaga, working in cross-functional teams helping to build the Quantexa Platform, our core Contextual Decision Intelligence offering. Our technology helps customers tackle complex challenges across fraud detection, financial crime, data management and more.

In this role you will:

  • Own the design, planning and delivery of entire features and epics end to end, ensuring they are delivered on time and to a high quality bar

  • Lead technical and architectural discussions, considering performance, reliability and security, and ensuring solutions work well within the wider system

  • Lead by example in AI-native engineering, helping to shape and drive the adoption of agentic tools and practices across the software development lifecycle

  • Build clean, well-tested and maintainable software, primarily in Scala, working with agentic tools to accelerate delivery and setting the standard for quality through code review

  • Work with Product Managers, Designers and Team Leads to shape upcoming features, contributing to estimates and reliable delivery plans

  • Mentor and support other engineers through code review, pairing and technical guidance, and take part in interviewing

  • Spot opportunities to improve processes, tooling and ways of working

Tech Stack:

Agentic tooling and automated workflows are embedded across our software development lifecycle, from design and coding through to testing, review and release, and we are building our own software factory, using services such as Claude to automate and accelerate how our engineers work.

We are hiring a Head of Technology for the garden3d creative collective, to lead engineering at Sanctuary Computer and garden3d in the era of agentic computer code.

Original job posting link

About garden3d

We are worker owned creative collective, innovating on everything from brands and IRL communities to IoT devices and cross platform apps. We share profit, open source everything, spin out new businesses, and invest in exciting ideas through financial and/or in-kind contributions.

Our client roster includes Google, Stripe, Figma, Hinge, Black Socialists in America, ACLU, Pratt, Parsons, Mozilla, The Nobel Prize, MIT, Gnosis, Etsy & Gagosian.

We’re the software team behind innovative products like The Light Phone & Mill, and we operate a global, decentralized community space collective called Index Space.

We think of our garden3d as collective for creative people, prioritizing a happy, talented, and diverse studio culture. We work on projects that bring value to our world, and we balance deep care for the work we do with a genuine curiosity about life outside of our jobs.

Sanctuary Computer - Development

At Sanctuary Computer we’re building a different type of technology shop – one that prioritizes close collaboration between the client and the craftsperson.

Our projects range from design-forward websites, to robust web apps, to native mobile development.

XXIX - Design

When we started XXIX in 2013, we set out to create a different kind of design studio and we’ve thrived because we continually ask what a creative practice can be.

We’re building a radically different kind of organization that values autonomy, growth, transparency, and shared responsibility.

Index - Community

Index is network of physical spaces all around the world, Index provides space for the exchange of knowledge and tools.

We nurture trust within the creative community through generosity and abundance of ideas and care.

garden3d TK — Media

At garden3d, we’re in the early stages of building an experimental media company exploring emerging themes related to the evolving landscape of technology, design and culture.

We aim to monetize this outlet, publish books, produce screenplays, and release music.

Plus, our partner organizations

Lightphone
Mill
IngredientAI

⛰️ The Head of Technology Role

The garden3d Head of Technology has one mandate: everything we build works, holds up in production, and gets built the smartest way available to us. We are a house of brands - Sanctuary Computer (development), XXIX (design), Index Space (community), USB Club (digital community), and the garden3d umbrella itself - and a lot of what all of them ship runs on software we wrote. Working in close partnership with our founder & president Hugh Francis, this person sets the engineering standard, and builds the culture that holds it.

You can be based anywhere. A lot of our people are in New York and there's some gravity here, but we already work across timezones and we would happily hire in Europe, Singapore, Chicago, or wherever you are. If you're the right person, we want to hear from you.

This role works with studio leads, developers, designers, project managers and clients across every garden3d vertical.

This person can move between a Rails migration, a Next.js app, a firmware release plan and an agent loop in the same week, and raise the bar on each of them.

They span all of garden3d, but their home base is Sanctuary Computer, where roughly 70% of their time goes. Our development studio is where the engineering standard gets set, and where it either holds or slips: architecture, code review, estimation, and the hardest technical calls on our biggest projects. The other 30% goes to garden3d's broader technology story: how we ship product for USB Club, build with agents across the collective, which tools and platforms we bet on, and what we build for ourselves.

They are also how we get better people. Our work is only as good as the engineers making it, so this person hunts for exceptional talent, sells them on us, and sets them up to do the best work of their careers. The ideal candidate looks at a worker-owned collective with four studios, an open P&L and clients like Google, Stripe, Brooklyn Museum and The Nobel Prize, and sees an engineering practice they can propel among the best in the world.

Responsibilities & Mandates

️ Systems that hold up

We build web apps, native apps, data pipelines, content platforms and connected devices for clients who can't afford for them to fall over. This person has engineered complex systems for a long time, and it shows in the architecture they draw before a line is written. They own the technical blueprint on our most important projects, and they make the hard calls on the rest: what to build, what to buy, and what to leave out.

All in on agentic development

The way software gets built changed, and we intend to be ahead of it. This person is already deep in it: loop engineering, agents running against evals, agents that open their own PRs, and the guardrails that make all of that trustworthy. They make agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer works, and they can tell the difference between a demo and a system a team can rely on.

Practical engineering

We strongly prefer convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms that let a small team ship a lot. TypeScript is the default language, Rails and Phoenix handle what they're best at, and we'd rather deploy to a platform like Render or Heroku than run our own infrastructure. This person practices value engineering: the simplest thing that works, built well, at a cost the client is glad to pay.

Code quality at Sanctuary Computer

Sanctuary Computer is where our engineering standard lives, so this is where most of their energy goes. They set what good code review looks like, keep our senior developers sharp on architecture and quality, and make sure that bar holds without slowing the team down.

Hiring and empowering the very best

They are a magnet for exceptional engineers. They know where to find them, how to convince them, and how to give them enough room to do their best work while still holding them to the standard. People who work for this person should get visibly better, and should say so.

Estimation, scoping and delivery

They make sure our teams can reliably estimate and story point the work ahead, and that we deliver at a pace that meets the dates we promised and protects our margins. When an estimate is wrong, they find out why and fix the process.

The technical voice in new business

Our clients include Google, Stripe, Figma, Mozilla and The Nobel Prize. This person joins new business calls as the trusted technical consultant, scopes the work, writes the technical side of proposals, and can explain a hard tradeoff to a client's CTO and their CEO in the same meeting.

Hardware sense

We're the software team behind The Light Phone and Mill, so a good share of our work touches devices. This person doesn't need to be a firmware engineer, but they understand how hardware works, where it constrains the software, and how to plan a project that spans both.

The garden3d technology story

Across the collective, they decide which tools and platforms we bet on, how every studio uses agents, and which internal tools are worth turning into products. When someone at garden3d asks "how should we build this?", this person has the answer, or knows who does.

Culture

They model garden3d's values of partnership, curiosity, and accountability. The engineers they lead do the best work of their careers here, because the feedback is honest, the recognition is earned, and the craft rubs off

 Special Projects

In addition to day to day responsibilities, here’s an idea of some of the projects this role may spearhead or support in coming years →

  • Making agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer builds, with loops and evals the whole team trusts
  • Setting the shared technical conventions every garden3d studio builds from
  • Landing the kind of flagship engineering engagement that changes what people think we do
  • Hiring the next generation of the engineering team, across every garden3d studio
  • Turning the internal tools and agents we build for ourselves into products
  • Partnering with the Head of Design so our own studio websites are as well engineered as they are designed

Qualifications

This is a great opportunity for someone looking to make a significant impact in a growing, dynamic company. Based on the responsibilities of this role, we think the right candidate has the following experience and skills:

Must have:

  • 12+ years building software, at least three of them leading engineers inside a studio, agency, startup or founder-led company
  • Deep experience engineering complex systems, shipped and run in production: distributed services, data pipelines, multi-platform products
  • A true technology generalist, comfortable across frontend, backend, data, infrastructure and native
  • A strong preference for practical engineering: convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms as a service over bespoke infrastructure
  • All in on agentic development: loop engineering, evals, and agents doing real work in a real codebase
  • Fluency across most of our stack: React, Next.js, Ruby on Rails, Elixir & Phoenix, Sanity, Postgres, Redis. You won't use all of it every week, but you should be able to review any of it
  • Experience as the technical lead in winning work: scoping, estimating and pitching to clients
  • A track record of hiring exceptional engineers, and of people who got measurably better working for them
  • Hands-on. This person can still write the code, not only review it (and will get on the tools when the need arises)

Nice-to-have:

  • A sense of how hardware works: firmware, embedded systems, IoT, and shipping software for physical products
  • Experience in a client services environment (a consultancy, agency or studio)
  • Experience in a Sales Engineer or Solutions Architect role
  • Open source projects they've started or maintained
  • Experience fostering close collaboration between design and engineering teams
  • Experience inside a worker-owned, open-book, or otherwise unusual company
  • A network in the engineering community: the meetups, the conferences, the people worth hiring
  • Interests in design, art, music, food or fashion. We find these people have a well rounded sense of quality

Who you are

The person we’re looking for is happy, relaxed and easy to get along with and appreciates a commitment to a culture of transparency, non-dictatorial leadership styles, and alternative methodologies. They’re flexible on anything except conceits that will lower their usually outstanding work quality. They work “smart” by carefully managing their workflow and team.

How we interview

After you submit your application, a member of our team will reach out. Our interview process starts with an intro call to answer any questions you have about the role and to learn a bit more about your experience and interests.

From there, we’ll follow up with a panel interview call where you get to meet a few members of our team, to openly discuss some of our challenges and ensure your skills and interests align with where we’re going as a business.

For qualified candidates, the process wraps with a reference call, and an offer to follow.

Compensation

This is a permanent leadership role. If this individual exceeds expectations in their first four months, we'll shape the permanent role together, with scope and compensation that grow as the studios and their revenue do. After a period of proven success (12 - 24 months), they become eligible to join our worker ownership program.

We start with a 4-month fraction trial contract, paid hourly between $110 - $175 p/hr pending seniority & experience. In the first few weeks of the trial, this individual will propose their own goals to define success in their trial, and present them to our leadership team for approval.

At garden3d, we believe that those who shoulder the most responsibility and create the greatest impact should be paid accordingly. This role greatly favors autonomous, competent & ambitious operators.

‍ How we work:

We believe that there’s a better balance between the poles of freelancing & full time, and for that reason we work differently to most shops:

  • Transparency & Ownership: We release out Profit & Loss statements to the community each year, open source our best ideas, and talk business & money with everyone in the company. We’re proud to run our business with integrity, and for that reason we share everything with our team & community.
  • 150% Carbon Negative: Our studio offsets 150% of the carbon we use to do business each year, dated back to our founding in 2015. We turn down work that is not in-line with our morals, and we encourage our peers to do the same. We have been certified climate neutral since 2021.
  • Strong Morals: Since our founding, we've turned down somewhere between $1mm - $2mm of work that didn't meet our moral standards. (Most of that was DTC brands that can't show a valid sustainability initiative).
  • Async & Decentralized: We use tools optimized for calm, thoughtful communication, and opt for async whenever possible. We fight hard to maintain our focus time.
  • Remote Friendly: Our company is fluent in remote work, making our workplace more decentralized, and democratized in the process.
  • Ideas & Products: In our spare studio time, we work to build our own open source or internal products to diversify & bolster our income. We create amazing technology products for our clients, so why not for the studio?

→ Read more on our Substack, over here.

How to apply

We’re excited to hear from you! ❤

Kindly submit a complete and thoughtful application, including relevant links that help verify your work experience and identity. Applications with missing or insufficient information will not move forward in the review process.

Our team carefully reviews every complete submission, and we truly appreciate the time and effort you put into applying! :)

About Arango:

Arango delivers a unified, natively multimodel contextual data platform that powers AI agents, assistants, and applications with the unified, current, and trusted business context needed to reason, decide, and act at scale.

The Arango Contextual Data Platform connects fragmented enterprise data with LLMs, copilots, and AI agents through a simplified architecture delivered out of the box. By combining graph, vector, document, key-value, and search capabilities in a single platform, Arango eliminates the complex stacks many organizations build to operationalize enterprise AI.

Trusted by organizations including NVIDIA, HPE, the London Stock Exchange, PSI CRO, the U.S. Air Force, NIH, Siemens, Transient.AI, Matpriskollen, and Articul8, Arango helps enterprises move from AI pilots to reliable production systems faster while lowering infrastructure complexity and total cost of ownership. Arango is a proud member of the NVIDIA Inception Program and the AWS ISV Accelerate Program. Learn more at arango.ai, LinkedIn, and G2.

About The Role

Arango is hiring a Customer Solution Architect to be the primary professional services interface between Arango and the customers deploying our AI product suite. You own the technical relationship end to end, from first discovery through production and expansion. Your job is to turn a customer's problem into a working architecture on Arango's multi-model platform and its GraphRAG and knowledge-graph capabilities, prove value early, and guide the customer's team through deployment and adoption. The role sits where solution architecture, graph data modeling, and applied AI meet. It suits someone who can hold a design conversation with a customer's chief architect in the morning and review a GraphRAG retrieval design with their engineers in the afternoon. Deep graph expertise is not optional here. It is the core of how Arango's AI suite delivers value, and the CSA is expected to be the customer's most trusted source of graph and GraphRAG design judgment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the technical customer relationship as the primary professional services contact across the full lifecycle: discovery, design, pilot, production, and expansion.
  • Run discovery with customer sponsors, domain experts, and operators to identify high-value use cases for Arango's AI product suite, and qualify them against real business outcomes.
  • Design target architectures on Arango's multi-model platform, including graph data models, AQL query and traversal patterns, and GraphRAG retrieval design tailored to the customer's domain.
  • Define success criteria, SLAs/SLOs, data access and governance requirements, and a phased delivery plan from proof of value to production.
  • Build reference implementations and prototypes that prove value early: graph schema, data connectors, GraphRAG pipelines, tool and agent orchestration, APIs.
  • Guide production deployment into secure, observable services alongside the customer's engineers, with CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, and proper testing.
  • Architect retrieval across graph traversal, vector search, and hybrid approaches (chunking, embeddings, ranking, caching), and orchestrate tool and agent calls.
  • Establish evaluation practices and iterate on prompts, models, retrieval strategy, and graph structure using offline and online metrics and A/B tests.
  • Design data pipelines (ETL/ELT), vector indices, graph ingestion, and metadata governance.
  • Define monitoring for quality, drift, hallucination and guardrail events, latency, and cost, and stand up alerting and dashboards with the customer.
  • Architect role-based access, secrets management, audit logging, PII redaction, and content safety controls.
  • Meet customer compliance requirements (SOC 2/ISO 27001, GDPR/CCPA, HIPAA as applicable).
  • Produce architecture documentation, runbooks, and reusable patterns, and train customer engineers and end users.
  • Act as the voice of the customer to Arango's product and engineering teams, shaping the roadmap with what we learn in the field.


Required Qualifications

  • Deep graph knowledge (central to this role). Hands-on expertise in graph data modeling, graph query and traversal (AQL, or equivalents such as Cypher or Gremlin), graph algorithms, and knowledge-graph design for AI. Direct experience building GraphRAG or knowledge-graph-backed retrieval for LLM applications.
  • 5+ years in software engineering, solution architecture, or technical professional services, including building and operating production systems.
  • Strong applied AI and Python skills, with a solid grasp of data structures, systems design, concurrency, and networking.
  • Strong database skills across graph, NoSQL, key-value, and document models. Multi-model experience is valued given Arango's platform.
  • Hands-on experience with modern LLMs and tooling (OpenAI/Anthropic/Llama, Hugging Face, LangChain/LlamaIndex, function and tool calling).
  • Retrieval and vector databases (FAISS, pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate, or similar), and hybrid retrieval that combines graph and vector.
  • Cloud and containers (AWS/GCP/Azure), Docker/Kubernetes, IaC (Terraform/CloudFormation), and CI/CD.
  • Observability (metrics, logs, traces) and performance tuning for latency-sensitive services.
  • Excellent customer-facing communication, with the ability to lead technical conversations from the executive level down to the engineering team.


Nice to have

  • Direct ArangoDB experience, or prior work deploying a graph database in production.
  • Search and IR fundamentals (BM25, hybrid retrieval, re-ranking, ColBERT, cross-encoders).
  • Front-end or full-stack experience (TypeScript/React, Next.js) for light UI prototyping.
  • MLOps platforms and evaluation frameworks (MLflow, Weights & Biases, Ragas, promptfoo, DeepEval).
  • Model adaptation and inference optimization awareness (LoRA/PEFT, DPO, distillation, quantization, vLLM/TGI/TensorRT-LLM), enough to advise on tradeoffs rather than to hand-build.
  • Domain experience in finance, healthcare, public sector, manufacturing, or retail.
  • Security and compliance familiarity: data residency, KMS/HSM, private networking.
  • French government or industry experience.


What success looks like (6–12 months)

  • 2 to 4 customer deployments of Arango's AI suite live in production against agreed uptime, latency, and cost targets.
  • Measurable quality and business outcomes (task accuracy, deflection rate, cycle time) backed by evaluation and telemetry.
  • Reusable graph and GraphRAG reference architectures and connectors adopted by the broader delivery team and by customers.
  • Customer teams enabled and self-sufficient, with runbooks, documentation, and training in place, and strong satisfaction and NPS.
  • A credible field feedback loop feeding Arango's product and engineering roadmap.


Our toolset

  • Platform & Graph: ArangoDB multi-model (graph, document, key-value), AQL, graph algorithms, GraphRAG
  • Models & SDKs: OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta Llama, Hugging Face
  • Retrieval: graph traversal plus FAISS, pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate; rerankers (ColBERT, cross-encoders)
  • Pipelines & Orchestration: LangChain, LlamaIndex, Ray, Airflow
  • MLOps & Evals: MLflow, Weights & Biases, Ragas, promptfoo, Great Expectations
  • Serving & Infra: vLLM, TGI, FastAPI/gRPC, Docker/K8s, Terraform, GitHub Actions
  • Observability & Guardrails: OpenTelemetry, Prometheus/Grafana, Llama Guard/Content Safety, custom filters
  • Data: Postgres/BigQuery/Snowflake; Kafka; object storage


Location: Paris, France

What Makes Arango Special?

At Arango, we believe that AI is only as powerful as the data foundation. Our mission is to help organizations build AI systems that can reason, decide and act based on unified, current, and trusted business context at scale. We are helping define a new category of infrastructure: the contextual data layer for AI.

Working at Arango means:

  • Contributing to cutting-edge AI and data infrastructure
  • Collaborating with experienced engineers, marketers, and product leaders
  • Helping shape how enterprises build AI-powered applications


If you're excited about the intersection of AI, data, and social media, we’d love to hear from you.

The OS Integration team ensures Firefox works well with the host operating system and environment. We’re a distributed team with expertise in Windows, macOS, and Linux-based operating systems. Datadog's client SDKs run inside our customers' mobile apps and websites, and every Datadog client-side product depends on them, including Real User Monitoring, Session Replay, Product Analytics, and Feature Flags. We maintain 11 open source SDKs across Browser, iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter, Kotlin Multiplatform, Unity, and more. 

 

As the Engineering Manager for Client SDKs, you'll build and lead the team that makes it easy for any team at Datadog to ship into those SDKs safely: fast CI, predictable releases, a shared spec across SDKs, and tooling that lets engineers and coding agents contribute without waiting on a review queue. It's a rare chance to own a developer platform that ships in public, at a scale where small decisions reach a lot of customers, and to shape how Datadog builds client-side products in the AI-native era. Both the team and its scope are expanding, so there's plenty of room to grow.

 

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

 

What You'll Do:

  • Build, lead, and grow a team of mostly senior software engineers, hiring well and helping senior and staff engineers grow their impact and careers

  • Own CI and test infrastructure across the SDK repositories: set health targets, detect and quarantine flaky tests, and provide test frameworks that engineers and coding agents can run locally

  • Define release cadences and help customers adopt updates, managing breaking changes in SDKs that can't be rolled back once they're installed in customers' apps

  • Keep SDKs consistent through a shared specification, and remove the review bottleneck so product teams can ship SDK changes without waiting on a small group of experts

  • Partner with product teams such as Session Replay, Product Analytics, and Feature Flags, along with our SDK guilds and server SDK teams, to guide SDK changes from design to release

  • Build feature sets for new product capabilities and bring that to all partner teams

  • Bring AI coding agents into how the team builds, tests, and ships, and take part in business-hours release, hotfix, and support escalation duty (no 24/7 pager)

 

Who You Are:

  • Experienced in managing a team of software engineers, including senior engineers

  • Someone who has shipped and maintained SDKs, libraries, or developer tools that other engineers depend on

  • Strong in at least one of Mobile Platforms, including iOS (Swift), Android (Kotlin) , or Browser (TypeScript), and able to hold a technical conversation about applications development.

  • Knowledgeable in release engineering, CI/CD, versioning, and backwards compatibility

  • Able to influence other teams without formal authority and build alignment across product teams

 

Nice to Have:

  • Open source maintainer experience, especially working with outside contributors

  • Experience with observability, crash reporting, analytics, or OpenTelemetry SDKs

  • Familiarity with cross-platform frameworks such as React Native, Flutter, or Kotlin Multiplatform

  • Experience leading a platform or developer experience team

  • Experience using AI coding agents in your team's workflow

 

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you're passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.

 

Benefits and Growth:

  • New hire stock equity (RSUs) and employee stock purchase plan (ESPP)

  • Continuous professional development, product training, and career pathing

  • Intradepartmental mentor and buddy program for in-house networking

  • An inclusive company culture, ability to join our Community Guilds (Datadog employee resource groups)

  • Access to Inclusion Talks, our internal panel discussions

  • Free, global mental health benefits for employees and dependents age 6+

  • Competitive global benefits

 

Benefits and Growth listed above may vary based on the country of your employment and the nature of your employment with Datadog.

A software engineer today uses Claude Code or Cursor. A mechanical engineer designing the next jet engine still searches Excel sheets and asks whoever has been around longest.

The problems are open ones. Getting an agent to reason usefully about geometry, making 3D search work on real customer part libraries, and figuring out what the interface even looks like when an engineer asks why a bracket failed. Senior or staff level depending on experience.

  • CAD conversion as a real pipeline. It used to be manual and brittle. Turning it into production infrastructure meant writing a Python wrapper around a C++ SDK and making it reliable enough to sit under everything else.

Description

QuantumDiamonds (QD) is entering its next phase: with the start of production, we are evolving from a startup into an industrial company. This transition requires an operational foundation built on clean, lean and scalable processes. Join the CEO Office and play a key role in establishing this foundation. As a Process Optimization Intern, you will map our processes in Odoo, from purchase request to bookkeeping, streamline workflows that have grown organically, and automate manual steps. You will work closely with Finance, Procurement and Manufacturing, and your work will have a direct and visible impact on our daily operations.

Who we are

Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of TU Munich, QD leverages quantum sensors to rapidly capture three-dimensional current maps within multi-layer chips. Our strong, international team of over 70, including physicists, engineers, data scientists, and other experts, works side by side with major semiconductor manufacturers, supporting chip debugging and accelerating yield analysis. Backed by top-tier deep tech investors, semiconductor experts, and strategic public programs, we have ensured long-term stability, shifting from breakthrough to scale - and shaping the next chapter in chip testing.

Why join QuantumDiamonds?

Picture this:

  • Quantum sensors that see inside the most advanced chips on Earth, right where two frontier fields collide.

  • Nobel-Prize physics aimed at real customers with real problems, in production now, not someday.

  • Physicists, data scientists, and engineers building side by side, turning deep science into tools the industry actually runs on.

  • An international team that runs at hard problems for fun, where knowledge moves fast and so do you.

Still unsure about why joining us?

  • You'll get to build a company together with a brilliant and welcoming team on a product that has never been done before.

  • From Day 1, you'll own your own topics end to end and see the direct impact of your work on how the world sees QuantumDiamonds.

  • Our technology is the cutting edge of tomorrow, starting today and not in 10 years.

  • You’ll be part of a high-growth company backed by top-tier investors.

Let’s make the invisible visible!

 
 

What will you do

  • Map our end-to-end processes in Odoo, from purchase requests and purchasing to goods receipt, inventory, manufacturing and accounting

  • Analyze existing workflows with Finance, Procurement and Manufacturing, identify bottlenecks and fix them yourself instead of just reporting them

  • Configure and extend Odoo modules, master data and approval flows, and help decide how the ERP grows with QD

  • Take projects live that make a visible difference in daily work, for example barcode scanning in goods receipt and warehouse

  • Automate repetitive manual steps with n8n and connect Odoo to the rest of our tooling stack

  • Build AI agents with Claude that read documents, check data and prepare transactions

  • Document processes and train colleagues so new workflows are adopted and stick

  • Keep data quality high and help set up reporting that gives management a clear view of operations

 

What is expected of you

  • You are enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program in Business Informatics, Industrial Engineering, Business Administration, Computer Science, or a related field

  • You have experience with an ERP system, ideally Odoo

  • You understand processes in purchasing, warehousing, manufacturing, or accounting

  • You have experience with automation tools such as n8n, Make, or Zapier

  • Experience with LLM-based workflows or agents, scripting in Python or JavaScript, or knowledge of SQL and data modeling is a plus

  • Experience in a fast-growing hardware or manufacturing company is a plus

  • You have a hands-on mentality: you implement things yourself instead of passing on requirements

  • You are available for a full-time internship of 4 to 6 months and can work from our Munich office

  • Fluent English is required, German is a plus

Our benefits

  • Mission: At QD, we’re driven by more than just building great products - we aim to make a lasting difference. Joining us means contributing to meaningful work that goes beyond business as usual.

  • Impact & growth: This is an exciting stage of our journey, and your voice matters. You’ll have the chance to shape our culture, influence key decisions, and grow alongside a company that’s scaling fast.

  • Health & fitness: With a company-sponsored Wellpass membership, you’ll have access to countless gyms, classes, and wellness offers across Germany to stay healthy and active.

  • Team & culture: We believe the best ideas come when we connect outside the office. From regular off-sites to team events, you’ll be part of a collaborative and supportive environment.

  • Well-being & balance: We value rest and recovery. That’s why you’ll enjoy 24 vacation days plus public holidays to recharge and return inspired.

About us

QuantumDiamonds GmbH, headquartered in Munich, Germany, develops and manufactures semiconductor inspection systems based on quantum sensing. Spun out of the Technical University of Munich in 2022, the company uses nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond to map electrical current with micrometer precision inside advanced 2.5D and 3D chip architectures. Nine of the world's ten largest semiconductor manufacturers are engaged with QuantumDiamonds, with systems deployed across Europe, the United States, and Asia. The company is investing €152 million to build the world's first production facility for quantum sensing-based semiconductor inspection tools, supported under the European Chips Act.

Fluent English is required for this role: it’s our working language across the company. Version française en fin de document.

About Brickanta

Brickanta is the AI-native agentic platform for construction. Hundreds of AI agents take on the administrative heavy lifting across bidding, procurement, compliance and quality assurance, so builders finish projects on time and on budget.

We’re backed by Y Combinator, have raised over $8M from Northzone, Anton Osika and Mario Götze, and already work with some of the largest contractors and developers in the industry. We’re an early team and growing fast, operating like an elite sports team: maximum freedom paired with maximum responsibility. You own your work, you document what matters, and you win and lose as a team.

Having built the platform with builders in the Nordics, we’re now taking it across Europe. France is one of our first markets, and this is one of our first roles on the ground.

The role

Most enterprise AI dies in the proof of concept. Forward deployed engineering is how we avoid that: you sit inside the customer’s workflow — on site, in the bid room, in the procurement process — and build until the work actually gets done differently.

In a new market, that also means teaching our agents how construction works here. An answer can look plausible and still be wrong in the way that matters on a real project: a CCAP clause read the wrong way, a quantity that doesn’t match the DPGF, a DTU requirement that gets missed. Your job is to spot that and turn the judgment into evals our systems can measure.

This is not consulting and it is not a demo role. You ship product: take a real bottleneck at a real contractor, build the agent workflow that removes it, prove the outcome in numbers, and bring what you learned back into the core platform.

What you’ll own

Deployments

Own named accounts in France end to end: understand the workflow, configure and extend our agents against their real documents and data, and get them into daily use.

Evaluation and ground truth

Run our agents against real French workflows and judge the outputs on correctness, completeness and practical usefulness, not on whether they sound convincing. Turn edge cases and production failures into repeatable evals: reference outputs, scoring rubrics, failure taxonomies and expert-reviewed datasets.

Building in the field

Write code. Integrations, data pipelines, prompts, eval harnesses, automated graders and occasionally a whole new feature: whatever it takes to make the workflow work at that customer. Work out what needs human judgment, then engineer the rest away.

Measurable outcomes

Define what success means before you start, then prove it: hours saved, bids won, risks caught. Measurable results rather than technical milestones.

Feeding the product

Capture what only shows up in production here, from DCEs and DPGFs to how tendering and procurement really run, and turn it into datasets, reusable building blocks and roadmap. Each deployment in France should make the next one faster.

Who we’re looking for

Some combination of construction depth, technical depth and a liking for customers. The unusual profile matters more than the perfect CV.

Background

  • Real exposure to construction in France: site work, works management (conduite de travaux), cost estimating (études de prix), quantity surveying (métrés), procurement or quality.
  • Experience building and shipping software (Python and/or TypeScript, APIs, data pipelines, SQL), or the raw ingredients and the drive to get there quickly.
  • Strong analytical ability and a serious interest in modern AI systems. We operate as an AI-first company.
  • Experience working directly with customers, or a clear appetite for it.
  • Fluent English, since it’s our working language, and native or near-native French. No Swedish needed.

Mindset

  • You go to where the work happens — site visits, bid rooms, procurement meetings — instead of guessing from a backlog.
  • Extremely detail-oriented: you work through many cases without letting the quality bar drift.
  • Curious about why systems fail, not just whether they fail.
  • High ownership: you find the problem, build the fix and follow it into production.
  • You write clearly. At Brickanta, writing creates clarity and everything important gets documented, which matters even more when the team is in another country.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and with being the only engineer in the room.

Growth path

This seat is built to grow with the French market. You join part-time about three months into our launch in France, as the first customers go live, with the aim of going full-time as the market grows. From there the role grows with it: running the first deployments yourself, then hiring and leading a forward deployed team in France, and over time owning Brickanta’s technical presence in the country alongside our local commercial lead.

Few people get to build and scale an AI company in a new market from the start, with a funded product and team behind them. That is the opportunity here: take France from first pilots to its leading contractors and developers, with responsibility, compensation and equity that grow as the market does. If you would rather go deep than broad, the path also runs inward to core AI, evals and platform engineering.

Snapshot

Location

Remote in France, with regular time on site at customers. You start with onboarding at our HQ in Stockholm alongside the team, then come back regularly. Travel and accommodation are covered.

Start

First half of 2027, about three months into our launch in France. Part-time to start (or a similar flexible setup), with the aim of going full-time as the market grows.

Level

Mid to senior. We care more about what you’ve built, on site or in code, than about years.

Comp

Competitive salary and equity — you’re early enough for it to matter.

Ceci est la version française de l’offre. L’anglais est indispensable pour ce poste : c’est notre langue de travail dans toute l’entreprise.

À propos de Brickanta

Brickanta est la plateforme agentique AI-native dédiée à la construction. Des centaines d’agents IA prennent en charge le gros du travail administratif sur les appels d’offres, les achats, la conformité et la qualité, pour que les entreprises du BTP livrent leurs projets dans les délais et dans le budget.

Nous sommes soutenus par Y Combinator, avons levé plus de 8 millions de dollars auprès de Northzone, d’Anton Osika et de Mario Götze, et travaillons déjà avec certaines des plus grandes entreprises de construction et certains des plus grands promoteurs du secteur. Nous sommes une jeune équipe en forte croissance, qui fonctionne comme une équipe sportive de haut niveau : liberté maximale et responsabilité maximale. Chacun est maître de son travail, documente ce qui compte, et l’on gagne et l’on perd en équipe.

Après avoir construit la plateforme avec des entreprises du BTP des pays nordiques, nous la déployons désormais en Europe. La France fait partie de nos premiers marchés, et ce poste est l’un de nos premiers recrutements sur place.

Le poste

La plupart des projets d’IA en entreprise meurent au stade de la preuve de concept. Le forward deployed engineering est notre façon de l’éviter : vous travaillez au cœur des processus du client — sur le chantier, au service études de prix, dans le processus achats — et vous construisez jusqu’à ce que le travail se fasse réellement autrement.

Sur un nouveau marché, cela veut aussi dire apprendre à nos agents comment on construit ici. Une réponse peut sembler plausible et pourtant être fausse là où cela compte sur un vrai projet : une clause du CCAP mal interprétée, une quantité qui ne correspond pas à la DPGF, une exigence d’un DTU passée inaperçue. Votre rôle est de le repérer et de transformer ce jugement en évaluations (evals) que nos systèmes peuvent mesurer.

Ce n’est pas du conseil, et ce n’est pas un poste de démo. Vous livrez du produit : vous prenez un vrai goulot d’étranglement chez une vraie entreprise de construction, vous construisez le workflow d’agents qui le supprime, vous prouvez le résultat en chiffres et vous rapportez ce que vous avez appris dans la plateforme.

Vos responsabilités

Déploiements

Vous prenez en charge des comptes clients en France de bout en bout : comprendre leur workflow, configurer et étendre nos agents sur leurs vrais documents et données, et les faire entrer dans l’usage quotidien.

Évaluation et vérité terrain

Vous testez nos agents sur de vrais workflows français et jugez les résultats sur leur exactitude, leur exhaustivité et leur utilité concrète, pas sur leur capacité à paraître convaincants. Vous transformez les cas limites et les erreurs en production en evals reproductibles : réponses de référence, grilles de notation, taxonomies d’erreurs et jeux de données validés par des experts.

Construire sur le terrain

Vous écrivez du code. Intégrations, pipelines de données, prompts, frameworks d’évaluation, évaluateurs automatiques et parfois une fonctionnalité entièrement nouvelle : tout ce qu’il faut pour que le workflow fonctionne chez ce client. Vous identifiez ce qui demande un jugement humain, puis vous automatisez le reste.

Des résultats mesurables

Vous définissez ce que signifie le succès avant de commencer, puis vous le prouvez : heures gagnées, appels d’offres remportés, risques détectés. Des résultats mesurables plutôt que des jalons techniques.

Nourrir le produit

Vous captez ce qui n’apparaît qu’en production ici, des DCE et des DPGF à la façon dont se passent vraiment les appels d’offres et les achats, et vous le transformez en jeux de données, en briques réutilisables et en roadmap. Chaque déploiement en France doit rendre le suivant plus rapide.

Le profil recherché

Une combinaison de connaissance du BTP, de profondeur technique et de goût pour le travail avec les clients. Un profil atypique compte plus qu’un CV parfait.

Parcours

  • Une vraie expérience du BTP en France : chantier, conduite de travaux, études de prix, métrés, achats ou qualité.
  • De l’expérience dans le développement et la mise en production de logiciels (Python et/ou TypeScript, API, pipelines de données, SQL), ou les bases et l’envie d’y arriver vite.
  • De solides capacités d’analyse et un réel intérêt pour les systèmes d’IA modernes. Nous fonctionnons comme une entreprise AI-first.
  • De l’expérience en relation directe avec des clients, ou une vraie envie de le faire.
  • Anglais courant, car c’est notre langue de travail, et français natif ou équivalent. Le suédois n’est pas nécessaire.

État d’esprit

  • Vous allez là où le travail se fait — visites de chantier, services études, réunions achats — au lieu de deviner depuis un backlog.
  • Un grand souci du détail : vous traitez de nombreux cas sans laisser baisser le niveau d’exigence.
  • La curiosité de comprendre pourquoi les systèmes échouent, pas seulement s’ils échouent.
  • Un fort sens des responsabilités : vous trouvez le problème, construisez la solution et la suivez jusqu’en production.
  • Vous écrivez clairement. Chez Brickanta, l’écrit crée de la clarté et tout ce qui est important est documenté, ce qui compte encore plus quand l’équipe est dans un autre pays.
  • À l’aise avec l’ambiguïté et avec le fait d’être la seule personne technique dans la salle.

Perspectives d’évolution

Ce poste est conçu pour grandir avec le marché français. Vous arrivez à temps partiel environ trois mois après le début de notre lancement en France, au moment où les premiers clients démarrent, avec l’objectif de passer à temps plein à mesure que le marché se développe. Le rôle évolue ensuite avec lui : vous menez d’abord vous-même les premiers déploiements, puis vous recrutez et dirigez une équipe forward deployed en France et, à terme, vous portez la présence technique de Brickanta dans le pays avec notre responsable commercial local.

Rares sont celles et ceux qui peuvent construire et faire grandir une entreprise d’IA sur un nouveau marché dès le départ, avec un produit financé et une équipe derrière eux. C’est l’opportunité ici : faire passer la France des premiers pilotes aux plus grandes entreprises du BTP et aux principaux promoteurs du pays, avec des responsabilités, une rémunération et une part du capital qui grandissent avec le marché. Si vous préférez la profondeur à l’étendue, le chemin mène aussi vers le cœur du produit : IA, evals et ingénierie de plateforme.

En bref

Lieu

Télétravail depuis la France, avec du temps sur le terrain chez les clients. Vous commencez par une intégration à notre siège de Stockholm aux côtés de l’équipe, puis vous y revenez régulièrement. Voyage et hébergement pris en charge.

Démarrage

Premier semestre 2027, environ trois mois après le début de notre lancement en France. Temps partiel au départ (ou une formule souple équivalente), avec l’objectif de passer à temps plein à mesure que le marché se développe.

Niveau

Confirmé à senior. Ce que vous avez construit, sur le chantier ou dans le code, compte plus que les années d’expérience.

Rémunération

Salaire compétitif et participation au capital — vous arrivez assez tôt pour que cela compte.

Teton is redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology and a great product experience. As populations get older and staff shortages grow, healthcare systems are under pressure. Our mission is to decrease the cost of healthcare while improving the quality of care.

Our product enables care teams to intervene, prevent and operate more efficiently. Our ambient sensors in resident rooms capture activity, sleep, respiration, gait and more. These signals are used both to react fast to risk events, like falls, and for long-term health analysis that care teams can act on.

Teton is scaling fast, operating in the Nordics, UK, DACH and US. We recently raised a $20M Series A. Expect travel to the US to meet users and team members.

We focus relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, deploying solutions at speed that make a tangible difference for carers. We are an aspiring meritocracy biased towards action, always striving to raise the bar. If you are driven by impact, speed and leveling up, this might be the place for you.

If you are looking for a 9-17 job, perform best with structure and struggle dealing with unknowns, this is not for you. We believe close collaboration between a hard-working, high-agency team enables the fastest and most efficient iteration cycles, helping us build an impactful product that healthcare professionals truly love to use.

We're looking for an experienced Frontend Engineer to own customer-facing features from the first conversation with a care team to the feature running in production. Care workers rely on our product during every shift and care managers use it to follow up on their residents, on mobile and on the web. This isn't a ticket-taking role. You'll talk to users, cut scope, build the features, and check afterwards whether what you shipped actually made a shift easier. Alongside that, you'll help own the quality of how we build: the tests, pipelines and guardrails that let us ship fast without breaking what care teams depend on.

In this role, you will focus on:

  • Feature Development: Own features end-to-end, from design discussions through implementation to production rollout across multiple markets and languages, on the web app, the mobile app and the APIs behind them.

  • Customer Insight: Talk to care staff and our customer success team every week, visit care facilities, and turn what you hear into clearly scoped product changes. Come with ideas, sketch the solution, and push it forward.

  • Code Quality & Guardrails: Help own code quality across the frontend. Improve our CI/CD pipelines and automated tests, keep the infrastructure scalable, and build the guardrails that let AI coding agents contribute safely.

  • Backend & APIs: Work with the APIs, data models and services your features need. You will not just consume APIs, you will help shape, improve and fix the systems behind them.

  • Quality, Privacy & Safety: Ship with care for health data: sensible access control, auditability and privacy by default. Use staged rollouts so new features never get in the way of the alerts care teams depend on.

Compliance remains one of the most manual functions in financial services. While most institutions still rely on fragmented tools and human-driven workflows, we believe AI is enabling a fundamental shift toward autonomous compliance. Our ambition is to build Level 5 Compliance: software that can gather evidence, investigate complex situations, assess risk and execute defensible decisions under defined policies.

Dotfile has grown into one of Europe's fastest-growing compliance technology companies. Today, 100+ financial institutions across 15 countries rely on Dotfile for critical compliance operations, with a rapidly growing presence in the US.

We recently raised our Series A from leading US and European investors and software operators. We're now entering our next chapter: investing heavily in product and AI, expanding internationally, and building the team that can make Dotfile the global standard for compliance infrastructure.

- Investigate production issues and improve performance, observability and resilience as the platform grows.

- Raise the engineering bar through knowledge sharing and improvements to how we develop and ship software.

- Contribute to the evolution of our platform as we build more AI-powered compliance capabilities.

About you

- You have 5+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of delivering and maintaining software in production.

Our team shared's mission is deploy AI agents to transform how patients and doctors connect

We believe healthcare shouldn't be defined by missed calls, endless waiting lines, and overwhelmed staff. Patients and professionals deserve better.

Vocca builds AI voice agents that answer every call instantly, schedule and reschedule appointments, and free up staff to focus on what matters most: care.

Already trusted by 15 000+ providers, we're transforming the patient-provider relationship, one call at a time.

Want to shape the future of healthcare?

Join us !

- Discover our company culture and values

- Here is a product teaser

- Eliott's interview for Welcome to the jungle

- Eliott's quick interview for Speedinvest

- Articles on our A round (techfundingnews, Maddyness, les echos, our blog)

The problem

Every medical centre has its own rules. Who can book what, with which practitioner, at what time, what to do with an urgent case at 6 pm. Today these rules live in prompts and in the heads of our ops team. Each new clinic takes hours of manual work, and the ops team is the bottleneck of our growth.

We are building the platform that removes that bottleneck. A scenario engine where the behaviour of the agent is structured configuration, not free text. A self-serve onboarding where a clinic connects its software and sets itself up. A dashboard where the medical staff stop executing and start supervising: the agent handles the volume, humans check what matters.

This is the difference between selling a service and selling a product. Every feature you ship here changes how fast Vocca can grow.

What you will do

- Build features end to end on the platform: backend, dashboard, and the internal tooling that deploys clinics. You own a feature from the spec with the ops team to production.

- Work on the scenario engine and the self-serve onboarding, the two biggest projects of the team this year.

- Ship to more than 1,000 medical staff who use the product all day. A small change has an instant impact, which is rare for a team our size.

- Learn from senior engineers who have built products before, and push them back when you think they are wrong.

Stack

TypeScript everywhere, backend and frontend (Node, monorepo), PostgreSQL, a design system written in code.
We are migrating our last Python services to TypeScript over the coming months.

How we build

- We use AI seriously. Agents in every workflow, Claude Max provided. A migration estimated at 3 months was done in 2 weeks. If you have built your own agent workflows, you will feel at home. If you want to learn, you will not find a better place.

- We ship the version that works, then fix the last 1% when it shows up. In healthcare that only works with rigour: tests, small changes, no untested refactoring.

- We talk every day with the ops team that deploys clinics and the sales team that sells the product. No silos.

Who does well here

- 2 to 5 years of experience shipping production software, ideally in a startup where you have seen what fast really means.

- A strong academic background (top engineering school) is a plus. A track record that speaks for itself works just as well.

- Comfortable in TypeScript and Node. The exact framework matters less than your fundamentals.

- You know how to scope and cut. Saying no is worth a lot here, because the AI always says yes.

- You want your work to be used, not just reviewed, and you like seeing the company grow.

Our first engineer arrived with one year of experience. Eighteen months later he was leading a team. We hire on trajectory, and no engineer has left since day one.

What we expect from you

First week

- Get onboarded on the stack.

- Ship your first improvement on the dashboard.

First month

- Own one feature end to end, from the spec with the ops team to production.

First 3 months

- Ship a piece of the scenario engine or the self-serve onboarding that clinics use in production.

- Know the product well enough to challenge a spec before building it.

6 to 12 months

- Own one area of the platform, with the ops team coming to you first.

- Take part in technical interviews and help the next engineers get onboarded.

Process: 4 steps, fast

- 45 min with Nans (Talent).

- 45 min with Pierrick, Head of Engineering.

- 1h30 in our office with the engineering team, with live coding without AI. We want to see how you think.

- 30 min with Hugo, CTO.

Then references and an offer. When the match is obvious, we have made an offer in 24 hours. You get feedback at every step.

Practical

- Paris, rue d'Alexandrie (Sentier), new offices.

- Hybrid 3 days at the office.

- Claude Max provided.

We aim to keep the process within 30 days. You'll receive continuous feedback throughout.

Why should you join Vocca?

- An entrepreneurial adventure, with a supportive, high-energy, execution-focused team

- A product already live, with delighted customers in a fast-growing market (healthcare automation, voice AI)

- A true scaling phase, with everything still to build

- Real responsibilities from day one

We hire people, not roles.

If you're excited about our opportunities but don't check every box, we'd love to hear from you. Everyone, no matter how underrepresented, should feel free to apply as it can only bring learnings or success. If you identify yourself as a woman: Did you know that research shows women often apply only when meeting 100% of requirements?

We'll be thrilled to receive your application!

Hey, I'm Adrian. I’m hiring a Senior Software Engineer to join the Data Search team at Modash.

Modash helps brands find, understand, and work with creators across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. More than 2,700 companies—including Stanley 1913, Sennheiser, and NordVPN—use us to manage and scale their creator partnerships.

Behind that product is a fascinating search problem: helping customers find the right people across 400M+ creator profiles and billions of media files. We’re combining large-scale data processing, traditional retrieval, vector search, multimodal embeddings, and LLMs to make that possible.

That’s where you come in.

Why we're hiring

Search at Modash isn't an internal platform or a support function. It is one of the core products customers use to discover creators.

The scale is large, the data is messy, and the search intent is often complex. A customer might be looking for creators in a specific niche, people whose content conveys a certain visual style, or accounts that resemble a group they already know. Solving that well requires more than adding another filter or calling an LLM API.

We need a senior engineer who can work across the full retrieval system—from data and indexing pipelines to embeddings, ranking, relevance, and low-latency serving—and take ambiguous product problems all the way to production.

You’ll join the specialised Data Search team and work closely with Data Core, Data Insights, product teams, customers, and company leadership. You’ll have real autonomy, but you won’t work in isolation.

If you want a feel for how we think about building software, check our Engineering Blog.

What you'll actually own

1. Make creator search meaningfully better.

You’ll improve how customers discover creators across 400M+ profiles and billions of media files. That includes retrieval, filtering, ranking, relevance, speed, and the product decisions that connect them.

2. Turn multimodal data into searchable intelligence.

You’ll build systems that generate and use embeddings from images, video, text, and audio at massive scale—then make those signals useful in a real customer-facing search experience.

3. Ship new search capabilities into production.

You’ll evaluate models and technologies pragmatically, understand tradeoffs around cost, latency, and quality, and move promising approaches from experiment to a reliable production system within weeks rather than quarters.

4. Own the system end to end.

You’ll help shape the problem, gather requirements, design the architecture, write the code, release it, measure the outcome, and improve it. Senior engineers here own results, not just implementation tasks.

What the day-to-day looks like

Here’s what a typical week might include:

  • Monday. A customer search is returning technically relevant but unhelpful results. You inspect the retrieval and ranking stages, identify where intent is being lost, and propose a measurable improvement.
  • Tuesday. Deep-focus time. You build a pipeline to generate multimodal embeddings across a large batch of creator content and test how the new representation affects retrieval quality and cost.
  • Wednesday. You work with Data Insights on a new in-house datapoint. Together, you agree on its definition, coverage, and data-quality requirements, then expose it in Search to give customers more ways to discover creators.
  • Thursday. You test a reranking model on a fixed set of real customer queries. You measure how much it improves relevance against the latency and inference cost it adds, then decide what's ready for production.
  • Friday. You review production metrics, investigate a relevance regression, and share what you learned with the team. The fix may be in the model, the data, the query logic, or the product itself—you follow the evidence.

We keep meetings purposeful and protect time for deep work. You’ll have a short standup, close collaboration when it helps, and plenty of space to design, build, optimise, and launch.

Requirements

What you've done before

  • Built large-scale data or backend products. You have solid experience working with systems where volume, latency, reliability, and cost all matter.
  • Shipped products from concept to production. You’ve owned scoping, architecture, implementation, release, measurement, and iteration—not just one layer of the solution.
  • Designed distributed systems. You can reason clearly about throughput, failure modes, data flow, scalability, and operational tradeoffs.
  • Built LLM-powered or agentic features in production. You understand the practical differences between models and can balance capability against latency and cost.
  • Worked autonomously on ambiguous problems. You know how to gather requirements, ask useful questions, and turn incomplete context into forward motion.
  • Communicated clearly across teams. You can explain technical tradeoffs to engineers and non-engineers, give direct feedback, and collaborate without creating unnecessary process.
  • Worked in a fast-moving product environment. You’re comfortable learning quickly, shipping incrementally, and changing direction when the evidence does.

Bonus points if you’ve worked with multimodal embeddings, vector databases, semantic search, ranking algorithms, model deployment, self-hosted models, or GPU infrastructure. Curiosity about the creator economy helps too, but we’ll get you up to speed.

Our stack

  • AWS and GCP, with Pulumi for infrastructure as code
  • Python, TypeScript, and Node.js
  • PySpark on AWS EMR
  • Airflow
  • Milvus Vector DB through Zilliz
  • Elasticsearch
  • LLM batch APIs
  • Apache Iceberg
  • SageMaker, DynamoDB, S3, Glue, Kinesis, Lambda, ECS, and Aurora
  • Slack, GitHub, Linear, Notion, and Cursor

The interview process

We move quickly and can complete the process in under a week:

  1. Intro chat

Annual salary range is 100,000€ - 130,000€ for this role. We hire across Europe, so the exact number depends on your location, employment type, skills, and experience.
  • Flexible hours ⏱ We care about outcomes, not when you log on.
  • Unlimited paid vacation 🌴 If you’re rested and happy, you do better work. Take what you need.
  • Personal development support 🧠 Courses, books, and conferences are on us when they help you grow.
  • Real ownership 💡 Take difficult search problems from idea to production without layers of unnecessary process.
  • Regular offsites ✈️ We’re remote-first, but we make time to connect, collaborate, and have fun together in person.

2,700+ companies like Stanley 1913, Sennheiser, and NordVPN already use Modash to manage and scale their influencer marketing work. And we're just getting started. Over the coming decade, brand investment in creators will continue to boom, and Modash will be at the centre of it all.

Europe's plants run on gas, power, heat and steam – and all of them are being rebuilt at the same time. The hard part isn't ambition, it's arithmetic: which asset to buy, when to run it, what to hedge. Europe's largest companies (~2% of total energy demand) answer these questions with our Energy OS: a digital twin of the site, an optimizer that plans it, and agents that operate it.

The optimizer is yours. Twenty-year investment decisions, quarter-hourly dispatch, real tariffs, real market rules. You report directly to the CTO – and nobody stands between your model and the plant it runs on.

Tasks

Optimization Models End-to-End: Own capacity expansion planning over multi-year horizons, dispatch at quarter-hour resolution, and MIP production scheduling with sequence-dependent setup times.

Model Physics & Contracts: Storage, thermal networks, transmission, flexibility, self-consumption, minimum part loads, start-up costs – formulate what reality actually demands.

Make It Solve: Tighten big-Ms, scale models cleanly, decide where decomposition earns its complexity – and where it doesn't.

Smart Data Reduction: Time series clustering, extreme periods, segmentation and aggregation – without accuracy quietly disappearing.

Regulation into Constraints: Model grid fees, levies, tariffs, balancing power and intraday trading per country, and understand what they do to the objective function.

Prove It's Right: Test cases on real customer systems, fixtures that catch regressions, and infeasibility output an engineer can actually diagnose.

Interface & Production: Define inputs and outputs with the Product Engineers; own the runs on Kubernetes – solve time, memory and cost are your numbers.

Explain to the Customer: When a customer questions a schedule, you're the one who can say why the model chose it.

Requirements

Education & Background: Degree in mathematics, operations research, computer science, physics, energy systems engineering, business mathematics or a comparable STEM qualification.

Optimization: Deep familiarity with LP and MILP and the craft around it – formulation strength, relaxations, warm starts, solver behavior.

Practice over Papers: You've taken a model from formulation to production that others depended on.

Code & Solvers: Strong Julia – or strong Python/C++ and a real appetite to learn Julia (JuMP) fast. Hands-on with Gurobi or HiGHS, including reading logs and knowing when to reformulate instead of tuning.

Data Sense & Engineering: Comfortable with long time series, unit and sign conventions; tests, version control, code review and CI are second nature.

AI-Native: Claude Code, agents and subagents are part of your daily loop – a requirement, not a plus.

High Ownership, Low Ceremony: You take on the unclear. Energy domain knowledge helps but isn't required.

Nice to have: Stochastic or robust optimization, Benders or column generation, unit commitment, energy market modeling.

Benefits

Share in the Success: Competitive base salary plus equity – we set your level during the process, not based on your CV.

Top-Tier Venture Capital Network: Direct access to the Point 9 and Earlybird networks – including formats for sparring, mentoring and further education.

Unforgettable Team Offsites (Workation): Once a year, the whole team goes on a workation. Including exclusive exchanges with our Visionary Voices (e.g. Robert Habeck, Kitty Mayo, James Vincent).

Corporate Health: Full flexibility for your fitness and health with Urban Sports Club.

Out to the Plant: Seeing the boiler you modeled changes how you build the product.

Our stack: Julia with JuMP on Gurobi and HiGHS, forecasting in Python, the product in TypeScript (Vue, Node, PostgreSQL), Google Cloud with Kubernetes for optimization jobs, GitLab CI, agents on LangGraph.

Small team, no layers between you and the decision. A model change that lands on Tuesday is in front of the customer on Thursday. In-person onboarding, then hybrid from Munich, Düsseldorf or Münster.
